entries.plain: The outer container of a web page. Everything the browser reads goes inside it.
The part of the page that describes it: title, character set, styles and scripts. It is not shown as page content.
The visible part of the page. Headings, paragraphs, images and buttons live here.
A generic box used to group other elements so you can style or arrange them together.
A small inline container for a piece of text or content, usually so part of a line can be styled.
A paragraph of text. Browsers add space above and below it.
The most important heading on the page. h2 to h6 are progressively smaller section headings.
A link. The href attribute says where clicking it goes.
Shows an image. The src attribute points at the image file and alt describes it for screen readers.
A bulleted list. Put each item in an li element inside it.
One item inside a ul or ol list.
A clickable button. JavaScript can listen for its click and react.
Loads JavaScript into the page, either inline or from a src file.
In the head, links an external file such as a stylesheet or icon to the page.
Describes the page to the browser, for example its character set or how mobile screens should scale it.
A label you give one or more elements so CSS and JavaScript can find and style them.
A unique name for one element on the page. JavaScript often uses it to find that exact element.
The destination of a link, or the file a stylesheet should load.
The address of a file an element should load, such as an image or a script.
